question: Recent years have seen an intensification of the role of the Organization of Turkic States (OTS), which seems to be evolving into a tool of geopolitical influence for Türkiye, both in Central Asia and in the wider Eastern Mediterranean region.

Of particular concern is Ankara’s attempt to leverage the OTS to promote political positions at odds with international law and EU interests, including actions undermining the sovereignty and territorial integrity of an EU Member State, the Republic of Cyprus.

At the same time, some OTS member or observer states maintain close political and economic relations with the EU, raising questions about the coherence and credibility of European foreign policy. Can the Commission answer the following: 1.
How does it assess the growing geopolitical role of the OTS and its use by Türkiye as a means of exerting influence against the EU’s interests?

How does it ensure that EU cooperation with states involved in the OTS does not lead – directly or indirectly – to the legitimisation of illegal actions or of narratives that violate international law and UN resolutions?
Does it intend to strengthen political dialogue and terms of cooperation with non-EU countries, making respect for the sovereignty and rights of all EU Member States a clear precondition?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (25.2.2026) The EU has repeatedly made clear that it recognises only the Republic of Cyprus as a subject of international law, in accordance with the respective United Nations Security Council (UNSC) resolutions1.

It has also actively expressed its concerns to the members of the Organisation of Turkic States (OTS), at all levels, and continues to call upon OTS members to refrain from actions that might imply the recognition of the so-called, internationally not recognised, Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus.

The EU remains fully committed to ensuring that the UNSC resolutions and generally recognised principles and norms of international law, particularly with respect to the sovereignty, independence and territorial integrity of states, are fully upheld.

In this context, the EU recalls the commitment of the Central Asian partners to the sovereignty and territorial integrity of all states within the framework of all international and regional fora, and to refrain from taking any steps that run contrary to those principles.

The EU also recalls the reaffirmation of the strong commitment of the Central Asian partners to the relevant UNSC resolutions 541(1983)2 and 550(1984)3. Respect of these international principles remain essential to the enhancement of EU-Central Asia relations4.
